evidence.why: Attempt arithmetic, polling, read errors, rejection and final error replacement.

facts.rationale: Corrects the claim that unreadable replies permit another attempt and preserves the exact counter/error guards.
facts.value: Initializes the reply identifier to -1 and the signed attempt counter from unsigned p2 + 1; ordinary configured retry counts permit one initial transmission plus p2 retries. After a successful send, p3 selects indefinite polling or a counter threshold of 79,999,980 unsuccessful polls, with the counter reset per transmission. Commands below kDSReplyACK are processed without consuming a send attempt. Short, non-ACK or error-status replies are released and can retry while error remains kNoError. Command/error-byte read failures also release the candidate but prevent further attempts, as do send failures. A valid ACK/no-error buffer is retained for the caller. Any terminal state with identifier -1 returns kWaitACKError, overriding earlier errors.

evidence.why: Request serialization, conditional copy, length replacement and unconditional accumulation.

facts.rationale: Preserves supported serialization knowledge while removing the unsupported actual-transferred-byte guarantee.
facts.value: Splits the requested count into request chunks of at most 0x800 bytes. Each message contains a read/write command byte, 32-bit handle, 16-bit requested length and, for writes, payload bytes. Reply mode parses an I/O-result byte and 16-bit returned length after the two ACK bytes; reads reconcile that length with the packet payload and copy only when it does not exceed the requested chunk. A returned-length mismatch replaces the iteration length and stops further chunks. Each iteration unconditionally adds its current length to the accumulated count, even after local failures; an oversized read reply can therefore be counted without being copied. The accumulated value is written to count and the local DSError is returned separately from io_result.

evidence.why: Concrete signature and all parameter/output branches.

facts.rationale: Corrects output-role overstatements and distinguishes remote status from locally synthesized status.
facts.value: DSError TRKSuppAccessFile(u32 file_handle, u8* data, size_t* count, u8* io_result, bool need_reply, bool read). data supplies write bytes or receives read bytes in reply mode. count supplies the requested size and receives accumulated iteration lengths, not guaranteed successfully transferred bytes. io_result is initialized to success and receives reply status, with local length checks able to replace zero by numeric 1. need_reply selects synchronous request/reply versus one-way sending; read selects the command and payload direction. Null data or zero requested count returns before updating the outputs; count and io_result pointers are not independently validated.

evidence.why: File-transfer bookkeeping and accepted/rejected reply-buffer lifetimes.

facts.rationale: Corrects the same completed-count overstatement at translation-unit scope while preserving buffer flow and ownership.
facts.value: Accepts a file handle, byte buffer, requested count, reply requirement and direction. Requests use chunks of at most 0x800 bytes, serialized as command, handle, length and optional write payload. Reply mode obtains a retained ACK buffer through TRKRequestSend, parses I/O status and returned length, conditionally copies read payload, and releases the reply buffer. Outgoing buffers are released after each iteration. Caller outputs receive the accumulated iteration lengths and I/O status, including locally synthesized status 1 for selected length inconsistencies. The count is not guaranteed completed bytes because accumulation is unconditional after failures and oversized read replies may be counted without copying.
